content_units: Office Karaoke Shortlist for a Mixed Group

A crowd-friendly 18-song set built for 8 coworkers: mostly English, widely recognizable for ages 25–50, clean lyrics, and easy enough for casual singers. The mix is balanced across pop, rock, and nostalgic singalongs, with energy rising naturally through the night.
18 Songs by Moment in the Night
1.   I Wanna Dance with Somebody   — Whitney Houston
- Great for getting the room involved from line one.
2.   Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go   — Wham!
- Bright, playful, and easy to clap along with.
- Works well for a group start.
3.   Valerie   — Mark Ronson ft. Amy Winehouse
- Best early, when energy is rising.
- Perfect for coworkers who want fun over vocal accuracy.
7.   Livin’ on a Prayer   — Bon Jovi
- Best done as a semi-group lead rather than solo.
8.   I’m a Believer   — Smash Mouth / The Monkees
- Cheerful, simple, and familiar across generations.
- Short phrases make it easy to carry.
9.   Build Me Up Buttercup   — The Foundations
- Easier than many current pop songs.
- Fun theatrical duet without demanding vocals.
12.   Islands in the Stream   — Kenny Rogers & Dolly Parton
13.   Don’t Go Breaking My Heart   — Elton John & Kiki Dee
- Gentle tempo and low vocal difficulty.
- Good calmer reset before the final run.
- Ideal for getting everyone back on the floor.
- The ending section turns into a full-room anthem.
- One of the safest big-finish karaoke picks.
- Everyone knows when to jump in.
- A strong final song if you want a lower-key but memorable close.
Best Flow for Your Office Social
-   Start with 1–2 upbeat openers   so nobody overthinks the singing.
-   Use confidence-builders next   for coworkers who prefer easy choruses.
-   Drop in duets mid-set   to keep variety and reduce solo pressure.
-   End with 2–3 all-in singalongs   where the whole group can join.
Best overall picks for this crowd
-   Safest opener:    I Wanna Dance with Somebody
-   Easiest for non-singers:    Shake It Off
- songs that still work if pitch is imperfect
- a balanced mix of pop, rock, and nostalgic crowd songs
If you run the set in order, it should feel natural rather than random: energetic start, easy middle, fun duet section, then big shared finales.
